scope.frame: the fibre at one tau with B1653's residue coupling, a flat hypercharge line, and one covariant Higgs (B1691's H-cov)
scope.object: the three charged sectors' second-to-third mass ratios near the cusp, over flat lines w = alpha tau + beta/2
scope.hypotheses: Lambda's frame; the Higgs's direction a covariant section (four sections tested); one Higgs for the three sectors (the bound then applies to every pair; with two Higgs fields, to the pair sharing one); no data

claim_one_line: THE CUSP WITH A TWISTED LINE PER SECTOR (P-169, part 1): with a flat hypercharge line on the fibre and one covariant Higgs, B1653's residue coupling and B1645's closed form agree (18 |q|^(1/2) without the line), the line keeps the m2/m3 exponent 1/2 in every sector, and it splits the three sectors' second-to-third hierarchies only by a coefficient that lies in [1, 4]: at Im tau = 14 over 484 lines the largest spread is 3.99999993 (generic factors 1, 2, 4; 4/3 and 8/3 at isolated tie lines; the line's real part never matters), at Im tau = 1.5, 2, 3 over four sections it is 3.01, 3.60, 3.92, and at W60's half-period line the sectors coincide (the d-e wall at the selected state); the reason is that m2/m3 depends only on the residue doublets' directions, which tend to basis lines except at ties. So in this frame a flat line can make the sectors' 2-3 hierarchies differ by at most four; the comparison with data is P-241, sealed first. 0 of 19. [CORRECTED 2026-10-21: the bound of four is B1653's point coupling, the large-L limit; at the canonical end of order one the spread exceeds four (7.7-10.8 at B1695's best point).]
weave_or_thread: weave (every sector on one fibre under one line)
